newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: KWAZULU-NATAL TEXTILES HARD HIT BY S.AFRICA STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: KWAZULU-NATAL TEXTILES HARD HIT BY S.AFRICA STRIKE.

text.p: The textile industry in South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal province was hardest hit by the one-day strike called to protest against new labour legislation, the Durban Chamber of Commerce and Industry said on Monday.
"Our members have reported a 50 to 75 percent stayaway with the textile industries being affected quite badly as were the engineering companies," chamber spokesman Neil McGregor told Reuters.
He said the chamber felt the strike was unnecessary and could harden the attitude of business towards labour.
"It is questionable whether today's action will make us change our views or not. It could even lead to a hardening of our attitude towards labour's demands," he said.

The Congress of South African Trade Unions, with 1.9 million members, called the strike to back demands for a 40-hour working week, six months maternity leave, double pay for Sunday and the minimum age for employment to be set at 18 years.
